edit_from_base: '0.1 s of coyote time' -> '2 s of coyote time'
prompt: Make the jump feel forgiving: add 2 s of coyote time and a 0.1 s jump buffer.

config.plan_model: Agent-tool model parameter 'sonnet' (Claude Code sub-agent; the harness did not report the resolved model id)
config.how: one fresh general-purpose sub-agent per plan, reads a job file with project brief + the developer prompt, writes numbered plan (<=8 steps, no code) via Write; not Claude Code plan mode

plans.text:
1. Read player.gd in full to learn how gravity, ground detection, jump input, and velocity are currently handled, and note any existing timers or state flags.
2. Check whether the requested 2 s coyote time is a typo, since typical values are about 0.1 to 0.2 s and 2 s would allow jumping long after leaving a ledge; confirm with the developer or, if unreachable, implement it as an easily changed exported value and flag the concern.
3. Add two tunable exported settings to the Player script (coyote time and jump buffer time) so they can be adjusted in the Inspector without editing logic.
4. Implement coyote time by starting a countdown whenever the player is on the floor and letting it run down once airborne, treating the player as "grounded enough to jump" while it remains above zero; clear it immediately when a jump is performed so it cannot cause a double jump.
5. Implement the jump buffer by starting a 0.1 s countdown when the jump button is pressed, and performing the jump as soon as the player is grounded (or within coyote time) while that countdown is still active, then clearing it.
6. Make sure normal jump behaviors still work: variable jump height on button release, jumping while grounded, and no extra jump when falling after a jump has already been used.
7. Run level_01.tscn and test the cases: jumping just after walking off a ledge, pressing jump just before landing, pressing jump too early or too late, and a repeated tap on the ground, adjusting values as needed.
8. Review the finished change for edge cases such as moving platforms, enemy bounces, and any other code that sets velocity or jump state, then summarize the changes for the developer.

1. Open player.gd and read how gravity, floor detection, jump input, and the physics process loop currently work, so the changes fit the existing movement logic.
2. Flag that 2 s of coyote time is far longer than the usual 0.1-0.2 s and would feel like floaty air-jumping. Ask the developer to confirm, and make the value an exported variable so it is easy to tune.
3. Add exported tuning variables for coyote time and jump buffer time (0.1 s), plus internal timers or counters for each, kept at the top of player.gd.
4. Implement coyote time: reset its timer whenever the player is on the floor, count it down while airborne, and allow a jump while it is above zero. Consume it on jump so a double jump is impossible.
5. Implement the jump buffer: when jump is pressed, start the buffer timer, and count it down each physics frame.
6. Trigger a jump when the buffer is active and the player is grounded or within coyote time, then clear both timers so one press yields exactly one jump.
7. Check edge cases: walking off a ledge, pressing jump just before landing, variable-height jump release, and no jump when falling from a jump already taken.
8. Run level_01.tscn and playtest on the platforms and both enemy encounters, then tune the values with the developer and confirm no other scripts depend on the old jump check.

1. Read player.gd to understand how gravity, floor detection, jump input, and velocity are currently handled in the physics process.
2. Flag that 2 s of coyote time is unusually long (typical values are around 0.1 s) and confirm with the developer, but implement it as exported tunable values so it is trivial to change.
3. Add two exported timing variables to the player script, coyote time (default 2.0 s) and jump buffer time (default 0.1 s), plus countdown timer state for each.
4. Implement coyote time by resetting its timer to the full value whenever the player is on the floor and counting it down each physics frame while airborne.
5. Implement the jump buffer by resetting its timer whenever the jump button is pressed and counting it down every frame.
6. Change the jump condition so a jump fires when the buffer timer is active and either the player is on the floor or coyote time remains, then zero both timers so one press cannot cause a double jump.
7. Make sure a jump already in progress cannot be re-triggered by coyote time (for example, clear coyote time on jumping) and that variable jump height or release-cut logic still behaves correctly.
8. Playtest in level_01.tscn by walking off ledges and pressing jump slightly early before landing, verifying both forgiveness windows work and that no double jumps occur.

2. Flag that "2 s" of coyote time is likely a typo for 0.2 s, since 2 seconds would let the player jump long after leaving a ledge. Confirm with the developer, or use 0.2 s and make the value easy to change.
3. Add two exported tuning variables, coyote time and jump buffer time, so they can be tweaked in the Inspector without editing logic.
4. Add coyote tracking: reset a countdown to the full value whenever the player is on the floor, and tick it down each physics frame while airborne. Consume it when a jump happens so the player cannot double-jump.
5. Add jump buffering: when the jump button is pressed, start a countdown that ticks down each frame. Perform the jump on the first frame where the buffer is active and either the player is on the floor or coyote time remains.
6. Update the jump condition to use these two timers instead of a direct on-floor check. Preserve existing behavior such as variable jump height on button release, and clear both timers once a jump fires.
7. Playtest in level_01.tscn: jump just after walking off a ledge, press jump just before landing, and confirm no double jumps or jump-on-spawn bugs. Also verify that the enemy bounce and any other code that sets velocity still behave correctly.
8. Tune the values by feel and report the final numbers and any assumptions, such as the 0.2 s interpretation, to the developer.

3. Add exported tuning variables for coyote time (2.0 s) and jump buffer (0.1 s) on the Player so they can be adjusted in the Inspector without editing logic.
4. Implement coyote time: while the player is on the floor, refill a coyote timer; when airborne, count it down, and allow a jump while it is still above zero.
